chapter: Dallas bands, Ray Charles and family
title: Segregated dances and carrying a show
summary: Smith played White and Black places, carrying a dance act and chorus girls in the Black venues; mixed dances became normal later.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: When you had the big band before that, you were touring around the area, were you playing only White dances, or Black

too? We played all of them, White and Black. We go and play for two or three days down there at a White place, and then we'd leave there and go and play at a Black place three or four days. They'd carry a show in there, but they didn't carry no show in the White place. They had me come all around here with it. Sometimes...
You say that you carried a show.
What do you mean? Like a dancer or something?
Yeah. Dancers. A dance act. Tap dancers. Two or three chorus girls. A singer. I always kept a girl singer.
Would you be responsible for organizing that?
And these would be local performers?
Oh yeah. All the people were here.
As you say, you didn't have the mixed dances.
Because nowadays you'd have it mixed. Or would you not?
Yeah. Oh yeah. They don't pay no attention to it
So when you had the 5- and 6-piece little band, you were playing for five years in this club, the name of which I've forgotten. What year are we up to, then?
